intro: The TCT Flying Saw Blade is designed for high-speed cutting applications in steel pipe and tube production lines. Equipped with tungsten carbide-tipped teeth and available with K5 coating, this industrial flying saw blade supports efficient cutting of moving metal tubes and profiles when matched with the appropriate flying saw machine and cutting parameters.

During continuous production, a flying saw machine synchronizes its movement with the advancing material to cut steel pipes and tubes to the required length. The performance of the TCT flying saw blade directly affects cutting quality, dimensional consistency, tool life and production efficiency.

offers a range of TCT flying saw blades in different diameters, thicknesses, tooth counts and tooth configurations to meet diverse industrial cutting requirements. R, P and ZYT tooth designs are available for different cutting processes and machine setups.

benefits: Tungsten carbide-tipped teeth are designed for demanding industrial cutting applications. With suitable blade selection and cutting parameters, they help maintain cutting performance and reduce the frequency of blade replacement.
K5 Coating for Heat and Wear Management

The K5 coated blade option is designed to improve surface wear resistance and help manage heat and material adhesion during cutting. Actual performance depends on the material, machine settings and operating conditions.
Used with a compatible flying saw machine, the blade supports synchronized cutting of continuously moving tubes and profiles, helping manufacturers achieve efficient fixed-length production.
Multiple Tooth Designs for Different Processes

R, P and ZYT configurations provide options for different cutting methods and production requirements. Selecting the correct tooth design is essential for balancing cutting quality, blade life and productivity.

select: When choosing a TCT flying saw blade for your flying saw machine, consider the following factors:
Material: Carbon steel, alloy steel or other materials approved for the selected blade.
Tube dimensions: Outer diameter, profile shape and wall thickness.
Blade dimensions: Outer diameter, bore diameter, blade thickness and mounting-hole arrangement.
Tooth configuration: R, P or ZYT, according to the existing cutting process.
Production conditions: Line speed, cutting speed, feed settings and cooling or lubrication conditions.
Cutting requirements: Cut length tolerance, end-face quality and acceptable burr level.
Machine compatibility: Spindle specifications, mounting arrangement and the original equipment manufacturer's requirements.
Providing these details helps our team recommend a suitable blade specification and avoid compatibility issues.
faq: What is a TCT flying saw blade?

A TCT flying saw blade is a circular cutting blade fitted with tungsten carbide-tipped teeth. It is used with a compatible flying saw machine to cut moving steel pipes, tubes or other suitable metal sections to a specified length in continuous production lines.
What is the difference between a flying saw blade and a flying saw machine?

A flying saw blade is the cutting tool that performs the cut. A flying saw machine is the equipment that carries and controls the blade, synchronizing its movement with the advancing material when required by the production process.
What materials can TCT flying saw blades cut?

They are primarily intended for compatible steel pipe and tube cutting applications. Suitability for a particular steel grade, profile or wall thickness should be confirmed based on the blade design and machine operating conditions.
What is the purpose of K5 coating on a TCT flying saw blade?

K5 coating is a blade surface treatment option designed to help improve wear resistance and manage heat and material adhesion. Actual results depend on the cutting material, operating conditions and machine settings.
How do I choose between R, P and ZYT tooth configurations?

The correct configuration depends on the cutting method, machine design, material dimensions and desired cut quality. Please provide your current blade model and application details so the appropriate configuration can be evaluated.
Are customized TCT flying saw blades available?

Yes. Customized specifications can be evaluated according to the required outer diameter, bore, thickness, tooth count, mounting-hole arrangement and tooth configuration. Final availability is subject to technical confirmation.
How can I extend the service life of a TCT flying saw blade?

Use a blade compatible with the material and flying saw machine, maintain the recommended cutting parameters, check blade mounting and alignment, and follow the equipment manufacturer's cooling, lubrication and maintenance instructions.
What information should I provide when requesting a quotation?

Please provide the blade dimensions, tooth configuration, steel material, tube diameter, wall thickness, production line speed, machine model and estimated order quantity. A photo of the existing blade label or a technical drawing can also help us confirm the specification.
